newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway June oil output slips below 3 mln bpd-survey.
newsitem.headline: Norway June oil output slips below 3 mln bpd-survey.

text.p: Norwegian crude output slipped six percent in June from May as scheduled maintenance cut production by around 240,000 barrels per day (bpd), a Reuter survey of oil companies operating in Norwegian waters showed.
Norway pumped an average 2.93 million bpd last month compared with 3.11 million bpd in May. The total excludes 169,543 bpd of condensate and liquids from the Sleipner East and West developments.
Adding to the reduction was an unscheduled outage at the North Sea Vigdis field and lower throughput at Snorre and the Norwegian Sea Heidrun development.
The biggest losses came at Norsk Hydro's giant Oseberg complex, which closed for eight days, cutting output by around 30 percent to an average 357,822 bpd.
Hydro also had an eight-day turnaround at Brage, which cut the flow there to 68,548 bpd from 104,939 bpd in May.
Statoil's Veslefrikk field was shut in for turnaround between June 9 and June 21, which reduced pumping to 28,638 bpd from an average 62,065 bpd in May.
Output at Elf's Froey field fell to 13,429 bpd from normal levels of about 30,000 bpd following planned maintenance from June 8 to June 20.

Oil and gas production at Saga Petroleum's Vigdis field was halted throughout the month following an unscheduled shutdown on May 23 after a gas leak in the compressor train. The company plans to restart the field in the beginning of July.
Vigdis produced around 50,000 bpd before the shutdown, but peak output is planned to reach around 75,000 bpd.
Saga will close the field down again for maintenance between August 25 and September 19 to coincide with a scheduled turnaround at the Gullfaks A platform.
Production also was lower at Saga's Snorre field due to work on risers -- tubes carrying produced crude from the seabed to the platform -- at the beginning of June.
Saga said output was around 200,000 bpd at the beginning of July due to too little well capacity, which the company is currently working on. Normal production at Snorre is around 220,000 bpd.
Statoil said the Heidrun development suffered a slippage in output of around 17,000 bpd due to problems with starting a new production well. Output in July had returned to normal, a spokesman said.
